about.title: Oroville Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases in Oroville often start with confusion — a surgery that led to complications, a delayed diagnosis, or medication given in the wrong dose. Butte County residents rely on a limited number of local hospitals and clinics, and when something goes wrong in that care, the aftermath can be overwhelming both physically and financially. California law sets specific rules for these claims, including a strict 90-day pre-suit notice requirement and tight filing deadlines under MICRA, so waiting to get informed can cost you options. We handle medical negligence claims and listen to what happened in your care. If your situation is one we handle, we'll explain your options and next steps. There's no charge for an initial consultation, and we only get paid if your claim results in a recovery. You don't have to sort through the legal details on your own.

items.title: We Understand the MICRA Clock
items.desc: California generally gives you one year from when you discover the injury, and no more than three years from the date it happened, to act — plus a required 90-day notice before any lawsuit is filed. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Medical Expert Review Matters
items.desc: Because a qualified medical expert is almost always required to support a malpractice claim, we know how to evaluate whether your case has the medical backing it needs.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But That Cap Rises
items.desc: California law places a statutory limit on non-economic damages that increases each year — we can walk you through how that applies to your specific situation.

items.question: I had a bad outcome after surgery in Oroville — does that mean it was malpractice?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California law is clear that a poor result alone doesn't establish malpractice; there has to be a departure from the accepted standard of medical care that caused harm. We can help you work with a qualified medical expert to determine whether your situation meets that legal standard.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered or reasonably should have discovered the injury, and no more than three years from the date the injury occurred, whichever comes first. There's also a required 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed, so it's worth getting information early rather than waiting.

items.question: Do you handle claims against Butte County hospitals or clinics directly?
items.answer: Yes — we handle medical negligence claims in the Oroville and Butte County area. We listen to what happened in your care and will evaluate the claim to explain your options and next steps.
